actions.note: submitted successfully; assess_action was attempted 8 times and every attempt finalized with MAJORITY_DISAGREE (see assess_disagreement_evidence below), so this action never reached ASSESSED. A follow-up execute_increment call against this unassessed action correctly reverted with 'EXPECTED: RiskClock gate is not executable' (tx 0x5bc682c55b3fe95fe35d08b0a7177f9e3de64815d168bee7f0002ccbdfddc171), proving the consumer's fail-closed gate check works, but no successful execution or replay-rejection was demonstrated for this action.

assess_disagreement_evidence.summary: assess_action(1) was called 8 times across three script runs. Every single call finalized with consensus result MAJORITY_DISAGREE, never MAJORITY_AGREE. Inspecting the receipts with `genlayer receipt <hash>` shows leader execution_result SUCCESS in every case; the disagreement is validators independently re-running the same GenLayer semantic risk assessment (gl.nondet.exec_prompt) and voting 'disagree' because they derive a different risk tier than the leader for this trivial low-risk action. One receipt (attempt 4) shows the leader node running primary_model 'policy:prd-mistral' while earlier successful policy transactions on this same account ran 'policy:prd-glm' -- i.e. different Studionet validator nodes are currently routed to different underlying LLM families, and those models disagree with each other on how conservatively to rate a benign INCREMENT_COUNTER action. This is the contract's designed fail-safe (RiskClock rejects a leader whose result the validator cannot independently reproduce within the allowed tier/variance) operating correctly on live infrastructure; it is real, not fabricated, evidence, and it is why this action could not be pushed further through the live test plan in this session.
